Summarise label health by class

Source: R/health.R
health_summary.Rd

Gives a dataset-level and class-level overview of label quality from the estimated joint distribution of given and true labels (see noise_matrices()):

  • an overall label health score, one minus the estimated share of mislabelled examples;

  • for every class, the estimated number and share of mislabelled examples, and the noise rates;

  • the pairs of classes that are most often confused with each other, which point to unclear class definitions or coding guidelines.

Usage

health_summary(x, ..., method = c("confident_joint", "calibrated"))

Arguments

x

Labels or an object holding labels and predicted probabilities. See Description.

...

Passed to label_inputs(): for example pred_probs when x is a label vector, or truth when x is a data frame.

method

Estimator of the number of label errors, see num_label_issues().

Value

An object of class label_health, a list with

  • score: the overall label health score;

  • n, num_label_issues: the number of examples and the estimated number of mislabelled examples;

  • classes: a tibble with one row per class, sorted from worst to best label_quality. label_noise is the estimated share of examples truly in the class that were given another label; inverse_label_noise the estimated share of examples given the label that truly belong to another class; label_quality is 1 - inverse_label_noise.

  • overlapping_classes: a tibble of class pairs with the estimated number of examples confused in either direction, sorted from most to least confused. Pairs that are never confused are left out.

References

Northcutt, C., Jiang, L., & Chuang, I. (2021). Confident learning: Estimating uncertainty in dataset labels. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, 70, 1373–1411. doi:10.1613/jair.1.12125

Examples

sim <- simulate_label_noise(n = 1000, noise_rate = 0.15, seed = 1)
health <- health_summary(sim, truth = given)
health
#> Label health
#> • Overall score: 0.808
#> • Estimated label issues: 192 of 1000 examples
#> 
#> Classes with the lowest label quality:
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   class     n num_label_issues label_issue_rate label_noise inverse_label_noise
#>   <fct> <int>            <int>            <dbl>       <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 D       147               45            0.306       0.525               0.388
#> 2 C       202               45            0.223       0.270               0.301
#> 3 B       281               51            0.181       0.253               0.257
#> 4 A       370               51            0.138       0.145               0.220
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: label_quality <dbl>
#> 
#> Most confused class pairs:
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   class_1 class_2 num_overlapping joint_probability
#>   <fct>   <fct>             <int>             <dbl>
#> 1 B       D                    71            0.0710
#> 2 A       D                    52            0.0518
#> 3 A       C                    43            0.0430
#> 4 B       C                    36            0.0364
#> 5 A       B                    36            0.0358
health$classes
